property_summary: A successful transferFrom call decreases the spender's reported allowance for that owner by at least the transferred amount.

For any spender, after approve(owner, spender, v) then transferFrom(owner, to, x) (with x<=v and adequate balances) the allowance allowed[owner][spender] strictly decreases by x in the correct contract; the mutant that omits decrementing allowed will leave the allowance unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any owner, spender, and transfer amount x (with usual admissibility), after approve(owner->spender, v) and a successful transferFrom by spender of x (x<=v and owner has balance), the allowance allowed[owner][spender] in the correct contract equals v - x, whereas the mutant that omits decrementing allowed leaves it equal to v for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any owner, spender, recipient and amount with owner having sufficient balance and an initial allowance v, after spender calls transferFrom(owner, recipient, amount) the reference contract always reports allowance(owner, spender) decreased by amount (i.e. equals v - amount); the mutant that omits decrementing allowed leaves allowance unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any owner, spender, recipient and amount where owner has enough balance and allowance v>=amount, after spender successfully calls transferFrom(owner, recipient, amount) the reference decreases allowance(owner, spender) by amount (result = v - amount); the mutant that omits decrementing allowed will sometimes leave the allowance equal to v, violating this rule.

For any owner, spender and approved allowance v, if the owner approves the spender for v and the owner then transfers tokens to the spender via transfer (not transferFrom), the spender's allowance must remain exactly v (i.e., non-invoked allowance stays unchanged); the mutant that fails to decrement allowed in transferFrom does not affect this rule, but we instead target that after approve(owner,spender,v) and a transferFrom by a different third party that uses transferFrom with spender as msg.sender the reference will decrement allowance while the mutant leaves it unchanged — thus the reference keeps allowed[owner][spender] == v - amount for all admissible inputs, and the mutant leaves it equal to v for some input.

After a successful transferFrom that transfers an amount less than the current allowance, the allowance strictly decreases but stays nonzero (i.e., it remains > 0).
